newsitem.title: UK: Copper ends LME kerb at 1-year high, others steady.
newsitem.headline: Copper ends LME kerb at 1-year high, others steady.

text.p: Base metal markets received a leg-up from firm copper prices during Wednesday LME trading as that market pushed up to new one-year highs, eventually clearing the $2,550 level.
Traders said the copper market staged an expected bounce from the outset, capitalising on a constructive technical close overnight, which provided the impetus to chase up to $2,550.
Other factors were a widening backwardation and a re-focusing on the OK Tedi concentrate shipment difficulties, although there were no concrete developments.
But given the Inco Sudbury strike, and possible lost copper output at Russia's Norilsk due to curtailed gas supplies, the market is sensitive to any disruptive factors.
"It has been a good performance -- stocks fell again (down 600 tonnes), the spread has gone out by $40 this week, although there is not that much physical business around," one said.
Cash/threes widened to a $100/105 backwardation, having been around $63 at the start of the week, with rates tightening from July onwards.
With the market perceived to be short and copper continuing to flow out of warehouses, a clear break above $2,550 should drive prices much higher in the short-term, traders said.
Last kerb business was at $2,553 a tonne, a $39 gain from Tuesday's kerb close.
Other metals were underpinned by copper, but advances were not particularly significant, even though inventories were down in all cases, bar tin.
Aluminium continued to make steady upside progress, which traders said was indicative of a solid technical picture. Inventories fell by a punchy 4,350 tonnes and the contango continued to shrink.
There was some resistance above $1,620, but with copper looking strong there is the possibility of prices being able to reach $1,640/50. Last kerb trade was at $1,626, up $9 from Tuesday.
The cash/threes contango was at $17/19, having been at $24 at the start of the week. Covering against the June date might see the spread into $15 soon, they said.

Nickel was higher, but somewhat rangebound, and may be trapped between $7,300 and $7,400 in the immediate short-term. Inco's strike continues to hold the market's attention. Last trade was at $7,350, up $60.
Zinc resumed its uptrend, but is still a little adrift of last week's 4-1/2 year highs. By the end of the morning prices were $8 higher at $1,371.
Tin followed the trend and gained $60 to $5,650. Lead was steady at $639.50/640, as was alloy at $1,480/85.
